evidence.estrutura: Sheppard pursued national suffrage legislation through constitutional institutions; no broad centralization doctrine.
evidence.representacao: Leadership of New Zealand’s successful women’s suffrage movement makes her exceptionally democratic and inclusion-oriented.
evidence.poder: Her constitutional petitioning supports civil political rights, while temperance activism accepted regulation of alcohol; mixed liberty/control profile.
evidence.imigracao: Immigration was not a defining issue in the core sources; keep moderate.
evidence.diplomacia: Foreign policy was peripheral; her reform methods were civic and nonviolent, supporting a mildly diplomatic orientation.
evidence.intervencao: No aggressive foreign-policy doctrine is documented; reformist pacific methods favor restraint.
evidence.economia: Her principal work was suffrage and social reform rather than ownership systems; moderate mixed economy.
evidence.controle: Temperance and reform activism indicate willingness to regulate social harms, but not economic command planning.
evidence.religiao: Work through the Women’s Christian Temperance Union indicates meaningful Christian reform influence without support for theocracy.
evidence.moral: Women’s equality was progressive, while temperance reflected restrictive moral reform; mixed but equality-leaning.
